[Musifold]{.mf-hero-title}

[Internalizing walks on the musical manifold.]{.mf-hero-tagline}

Music theory as geometry you can **see**, **hear** and **play**. Every idea
comes with an interactive figure: click it, listen to it, and walk through
harmonic space until the patterns feel familiar.

::: {.mf-hero-actions}

[View as slides](tutorials/fundamentals/fundamentals-slides.html){.btn .btn-outline-secondary}
:::

## Try it

Every major and minor chord is a triangle on this lattice, the *Tonnetz*.
**Click any triangle** to hear the chord and light up the three chords that
share two of its notes. Moving between neighbours is what smooth harmony
sounds like.

::: {.mf-widget data-widget="tonnetz" data-mode="explore"}
[Interactive figure: a clickable Tonnetz lattice. It needs JavaScript.]{.mf-noscript}
:::

### Music Theory Fundamentals

From the harmonic series to the Tonnetz: why some intervals sound stable,
why no tuning is perfect, how scales and modes are built, and why chords
resolve. With notes for violin.

### Guitar Harmony

Short lessons on the fretboard: the geometry of intervals across the
strings, where the chords of a key live, voice leading, and the
progressions that make music move.

[21 lessons · playable fretboards]{.mf-meta}
:::

## How it works

::: {.grid .mf-pillars}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
#### See it
Pitches, chords and keys drawn as shapes: circles of fifths, lattices of
triads, and fretboards.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
#### Hear it
Every figure makes sound, so you can check each idea by ear rather than
take it on faith.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
#### Play it
Exercises for the instrument in your hands, starting with violin and
guitar.
:::

:::

[Built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org). The figures are plain JavaScript
and the Web Audio API, with no plugins. Turn your sound on.]{.mf-footnote}
